findings.body: Raise: Functional. After machine B publishes a clean review for a newer PR head, a record refresh from machine A replaces B's published `ready` commit with A's older receipt commit, or with null if A has no receipt. `nextstep._item_readiness` reads only `record.ready`, so teammates then see the unchanged, clean PR as not ready. Worker question and answer refreshes can reach this path without a new close.
findings.title: Refreshing a PR from an older checkout erases newer clean readiness

findings.body: Raise: Functional. A human-merge wait started on machine B exists in the PR record but not in machine A's local events. When A resumes `forge work`, this call searches only local events, so it records no wait end. The shared record continues to show an owner wait after work resumes, and the board can report the item as waiting for a merge that is no longer its next action.
findings.title: Cross-machine rework leaves a published owner wait open

stop.reason: Owner chose narrow: fix the per-round git calls on board reads; questions on pull requests opened before this release stay local
